about: A fast .NET library for reading and writing Excel files with little memory.

prs.title: Durations from Excel keep their whole seconds
prs.broken: Time lengths read from Excel often came back a hair short, so 11 seconds showed as 10. In one test sheet 1541 of 5600 durations were off.
prs.changed: Durations are now rounded to milliseconds, the same way dates already were.
prs.matters: Reports and imports show the same times Excel shows.

prs.title: Durations of a day or more export as durations
prs.broken: A time length of a day or more was saved with a date format, so 36 hours showed as 1/1/1900 in Excel. Shorter ones wrapped around at 24 hours.
prs.changed: All durations are now saved with Excel's hours format, which counts past 24 and reads back as a duration.
prs.matters: Time tracking totals and job durations show correctly in Excel.

prs.title: CSV values with a tab inside stay in one column
prs.broken: The CSV reader split rows on tabs as well as commas. A value with a tab inside got split in two, shifting columns or crashing the read. MiniExcel could not read back its own files.
prs.changed: Rows are now split only on the separator the user set.
prs.matters: CSV files with tabs in notes or text load with every value in the right column.
